current_review_record.rationale: Qualified whole-amendment candidate: the literal $50 million reduction to the United States Emergency Refugee and Migration Assistance Fund is an independent exact Immigration & Border funding mechanism under existing standards. Preserve the Jordan prohibition and all eight cuts, reported $100 million emergency-fund baseline, availability/cap/transfer/urgent-needs conditions, literal fifth account and Global Health target. Section2601(f)/country-ban application remains separately qualified; no actual refugee/admission/spending result or component preference. Exact initial voice noes/demand/postponement and resumed recorded rejection are bound. Candidate only, independent review pending; not editorial acceptance or whole-passage247 closure.

active_authoring_action.short_description: H.R.8595 Jordan restriction and eight account cuts including emergency refugee funding
active_authoring_action.compact_description: The amendment would prohibit this Act's funds for Jordan and make eight named account reductions, including $50 million from the proposed emergency refugee and migration appropriation. It was rejected; country-restriction application remains qualified.
active_authoring_action.meaning: The exact Part A amendment No. 9 to H.R.8595 combines a prohibition on obligating or expending any funds made available under this Act for Jordan with eight separate reductions to amounts otherwise made available by this Act: Foreign Military Financing Program, $475 million; National Security Investment Programs, $500 million; Global Health Programs, $845.1 million; Security Sector Programs, $50 million; the literal printed account Funds Appropriated to the President International Military Education and Training, $50 million; Nonproliferation, anti-terrorism, demining, and related programs, $29.9 million; United States Emergency Refugee and Migration Assistance Fund, $50 million; and Democracy Fund, $100 million. These are named account reductions, not a finding that each amount is already a Jordan-specific allocation. The reported bill proposes $100 million for the emergency refugee and migration fund under 22 USC2601(c), available until expended, with an express exception to the statutory unobligated-balance cap and qualified authority to transfer excess-cap amounts to International Humanitarian Assistance. The amendment would reduce that proposed emergency-fund appropriation by $50 million; it would not repeal the fund or its governing authority. Section2601(c) concerns unexpected urgent refugee and migration needs that the President determines important to the national interest, with the statutory funding and committee-information conditions retained. Independent Immigration membership follows this explicit refugee/migration appropriation reduction, without treating every foreign-assistance or military account as an immigration mechanism. The country-wide prohibition and all seven other reductions remain part of the same exact choice. The printed Global Health reduction and the literal military-education account wording are retained, rather than replaced with the reported bill's differently stated Jordan budget-support allocations. The reported bill separately provides qualified Jordan support, including additional National Security and Foreign Military Financing minimums; those provisions are not substituted for the amendment's account list. Section2601(f) allows its refugee and migration assistance notwithstanding foreign-country restrictions; the interaction of that provision with the new Jordan prohibition is reserved for application review. It does not erase or make contingent the independent literal emergency-fund reduction. The initial question produced voice noes, followed by the proponent's recorded-vote demand and postponement; resumed proceedings ordered a recorded vote. The House rejected this amendment, 6 ayes to 421 noes, with 10 not voting. The vote therefore did not enact these cuts. No actual spending, refugee admission, recipient eligibility or displacement outcome is inferred.
limitations: Exact amendment choice: all eight reductions and the whole-Act Jordan restriction are retained. Support or opposition to this combination does not establish a separate position on each account or on Jordan, refugees or foreign assistance generally.

The $50 million emergency-fund reduction is explicit in the amendment and is compared with the proposed $100 million reported-bill appropriation. Amounts are legislative proposals, not actual spending or cuts enacted by this rejected amendment. Availability until expended, the express cap exception, qualified transfer provisions and governing urgent-needs/national-interest/committee-information conditions remain.

The $845.1 million cut is printed under Global Health Programs. The fifth account is retained exactly as printed; no account-name repair or reassignment to Jordan budget support. The separate country allocations do not show that all eight reduction amounts would be taken only from Jordan activities.

22 USC2601(f) and the broad country restriction require qualified application review; no conclusion that the new prohibition automatically overrides, or is overridden by, that existing notwithstanding clause. The direct account reduction supplies the domain mechanism independently.

Clerk amendment number 6 and Rules Part A number 9 are different identifiers for the same exact recorded question. Initial voice noes, demand, postponement, resumed order and final rejection are separately source-bound. Present and Not Voting remain non-directional when encountered.

This is a candidate under the established exact-mechanism standard, pending independent review. It provides no whole-passage247 interpretation, complete State-funding or full-issue closure, individual legal result, motive, enactment or editorial acceptance.

claim_source_map.passage: U.S.C. Title 22 - FOREIGN RELATIONS AND INTERCOURSE 22 U.S.C. United States Code, 2024 Edition Title 22 - FOREIGN RELATIONS AND INTERCOURSE CHAPTER 36 - MIGRATION AND REFUGEE ASSISTANCE Sec. 2601 - Refugees and migration From the U.S. Government Publishing Office, www.gpo.gov §2601. Refugees and migration (a) United States membership in International Organization for Migration; contributions to Organization (1) The President is authorized to continue membership for the United States in the International Organization for Migration in accordance with the constitution of such organization approved in Venice, Italy, on October 19, 1953, as amended in Geneva, Switzerland, on November 24, 1998, upon entry into force of such amendments. (2) For the purpose of assisting in the movement of refugees and migrants, there are authorized to be appropriated to the President such amounts as may be necessary from time to time for payment by the United States of its contributions to the International Organization for Migration and all necessary salaries and expenses incidental to United States participation in such organization. (b) Appropriations for assistance to refugees There are authorized to be appropriated such amounts as may be necessary from time to time— (1) for contributions to the activities of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees for assistance to refugees under his mandate or persons on behalf of whom he is exercising his good offices, and for contributions to the International Organization for Migration, the International Committee of the Red Cross, and to other relevant international organizations; and (2) for assistance to or on behalf of refugees who are outside the United States designated by the President (by class, group, or designation of their respective countries of origin or areas of residence) when the President determines that such assistance will contribute to the foreign policy interests of the United States. (c) United States Emergency Refugee and Migration Assistance Fund; appropriations (1) Whenever the President determines it to be important to the national interest he is authorized to furnish on such terms and conditions as he may determine assistance under this chapter for the purpose of meeting unexpected urgent refugee and migration needs. (2) There is established a United States Emergency Refugee and Migration Assistance Fund to carry out the purposes of this section. There is authorized to be appropriated to the President from time to time such amounts as may be necessary for the fund to carry out the purposes of this section, except that no amount of funds may be appropriated which, when added to amounts previously appropriated but not yet obligated, would cause such amounts to exceed $100,000,000. Amounts appropriated hereunder shall remain available until expended. (3) Whenever the President requests appropriations pursuant to this authorization he shall justify such requests to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, as well as to the Committees on Appropriations. (d) Information to Congressional committees The President shall keep the appropriate committees of Congress currently informed of the use of funds and the exercise of functions authorized in this chapter. (e) Continued availability of certain funds Unexpended balances of funds made available under authority of the Mutual Security Act of 1954, as amended, and of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as amended, [22 U.S.C. 2151 et seq.], and allocated or transferred for the purposes of sections 405(a), 405(c), 405(d) and 451(c) 1 of the Mutual Security Act of 1954, as amended [22 U.S.C. 1925(a), (c), (d), 1951(c)], are authorized to be continued available for the purposes of this section and may be consolidated with appropriations authorized by this section. (f) Restrictions on foreign assistance not applicable to migration and refugee assistance The President may furnish assistance and make contributions under this chapter notwithstanding any provision of law which restricts assistance to foreign countries. (Pub. L. 87–510, §2, June 28, 1962, 76 Stat. 121; Pub. L. 88–634, title II, §201, Oct. 7, 1964, 78 Stat. 1021; Pub. L. 94–141, title V, §501(a), Nov. 29, 1975, 89 Stat. 771; Pub.
